sections.overview: The Natural History Museum lists Evarcha falcata as an accepted British spider species in the jumping-spider family Salticidae.
sections.identification: Males are about 4.3–5.9 mm and females 5.0–7.7 mm; the male has pale lateral bands and curved brown markings, while the female is brown with pale sides.
sections.habitat: Its Palearctic range extends from Europe to China. It uses grass, shrubs and woodland; Czech records include clearings, heath and bog.
sections.diet: Species accounts consulted do not give a prey list specific to E. falcata; as a jumping spider it hunts actively rather than trapping prey in a capture web.
sections.behavior: The Czech arachnological database records this species across varied open and partly shaded habitats, but does not describe its courtship behavior.
sections.reproduction: The reviewed species accounts provide no detailed breeding or egg-sac description for this spider.
sections.ecology: The Czech checklist also records the close relative Evarcha arcuata; both belong to the same jumping-spider genus, but the sources provide no direct ecological comparison.
sections.conservation: The Czech Arachnological Society reports a Least Concern category in its national database; this is a Czech assessment, not a global one.
